newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2914 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2920 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai with buying active at the 8.2920 resistance level, traders said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2919.
The yuan opened sharply up at an intraday high of 8.2868 and fell to move in a narrow range of 8.2914 and 8.2916 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2918 late in trading.
Trading was more active than Tuesday with most business done at 8.2915, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan seemed to have hit bottom after closing at 8.2920 on Tuesday.
"Buying set in right after the market opened on Wednesday and persisted at around the 8.2920 level, pushing the yuan to close higher," he said.
A second dealer said the high opening was due to a single transaction and would have little impact on near-term trend.
"Despite the very high opening, most people believe the yuan will only move in a range of 8.2900 and 8.2920 in the short term," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2920 on Thursday.
The yuan closed down at 7.1340 from 7.1150 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0705 from 1.0710 against the Hong Kong dollar.
